question: As per Census 2011, what was the child sex ratio of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Census 2011**, the **child sex ratio** in India was reported to be **919 females per 1000 males** in the age group of 0-6 years.
 
• The **child sex ratio** is an important demographic indicator that reflects the number of girls per 1000 boys in a specific age group, typically under the age of 6 years.
 
• The declining child sex ratio has been a matter of concern for policymakers and society, as it indicates a preference for male children and the prevalence of **sex-selective practices.**
 
• The child sex ratio in India has been steadily declining since the 1960s. The 2011 Census showed a further decline from the 2001 Census, where the ratio was recorded as **927 females per 1000 males**.
 
• This decline is attributed to factors like **female feticide, gender-based discrimination, and societal preference for male children**.
 
• The government has introduced several schemes and laws, such as the **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act** of 1994, to curb sex-selective abortions and improve the child sex ratio in India.
 
• The **Betti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)** scheme launched in 2015 aims to address the declining child sex ratio and promote the education of girl children.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 919.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Child Sex Ratio (CSR):**

 
 
• The **child sex ratio** is defined as the number of girls per 1000 boys in the age group of 0-6 years.
 
• It is an important indicator of the **social health of a society** and reflects the extent of gender discrimination and practices such as sex-selective abortions.
 
 
 
• **Trends in Child Sex Ratio:**
 
 
• In **India**, the child sex ratio has been declining over the years. It was **945 in 1991**, **927 in 2001**, and further decreased to **919 in 2011**.
 
• This decline highlights the prevalence of gender-based discrimination and social biases in favor of male children.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Improve CSR:**
 
 
• The **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act**, 1994, prohibits sex determination of the fetus to curb female feticide.
 
• The **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)** scheme, launched in 2015, aims to address declining child sex ratios and promote awareness about the importance of girl children.
 
• Various state-level initiatives, such as the **Laadli Scheme** in Haryana, provide financial incentives to families for educating and supporting girl children.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impacts of Declining Child Sex Ratio:**

 
 
• A declining child sex ratio leads to long-term social and demographic challenges, such as an imbalanced population structure and increased gender-based violence.
 
• It reflects a deep-rooted societal preference for sons over daughters, which can hinder overall progress in achieving gender equality.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• Globally, countries like **China** also face similar issues due to their **one-child policy**, which resulted in a skewed sex ratio.
 
• Efforts at the global level, such as **UNICEF campaigns**, focus on promoting gender equality and reducing gender-based discrimination.
